To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the concentration of PAH in cocoa butter was affected by their cocoa beans’ drying methods; (2) the concentration of the carcinogenic PAH in cocoa beans was affected by their drying methods and the type of fuel; (3) the concentration of carcinogenic PAH was affected by the drying time and the drying methods; (4) the PAH concentration in cocoa butter extracted with whole cocoa bean was higher than that extracted with cocoa cotyledon.

1) PAHs contamination originated mostly from smoke during drying and small amount was formed during fermentation and drying, 2) Longer drying time promoted PAHs concentration, 3) PAHs concentration in cocoa butter extracted whole bean was higher than that extracted from cotyledon, 4) The highest risk of PAHs contamination during artificial drying occurred when there was a gas leak from gas separator, 5) Uses of artificial dryer using wood as fuel showed higher risk of contamination
In summary, our research is concerned with
the contamination of PAHs and their formation during cocoa drying process.
the effect of drying method of cocoa bean on the contamination and formation of PAH in cocoa butter.
the contamination and/or formation of PAH in cocoa butter as well as the effect of cocoa bean drying on the formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
benzo[a]-pyrene and other polycyclic aromatic compounds are genotoxic and carcinogenic (IARC,1993; Baer-Duobowska et al., 2002).
PAHs are carcinogens, which are present in the environment and can be found in food (European Union,2006).
benzo[a]-pyrene and DMAB can be used as a marker to indicate PAH contamination in cocoa butter and other foods (EFSA/DATEX, 2008; European Food Safety, 2008).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PAHs are carcinogenic and their presence in foods is a health concern, therefore, it should be controlled and minimized.
benzo[a]-pyrene is a marker of PAH contamination in food, but that it may not be a marker for all PAHs and it may not be the PAH that causes the most concern.
the presence of benzo[a]- pyrene in cocoa butter is not a problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of PAHs is not only due to the cocoa bean drying process, but also due to fermentation and drying.
the presence of PAHs can occur in the cocoa bean during drying process, which may be due to contamination of the smoke during the drying process.
the PAHs in the cocoa butter are formed during the drying process of the cocoa beans.
